channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Putin Proposes Summit with US, China on Ukraine, WSJ Reports
item.description: Russia’s Vladimir Putin proposed a meeting with President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping next month to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, the Wall Street Journal reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Euro Falls as Russia Risk, France Protests Dent Trader Sentiment
item.description: The euro fell against most of its Group-of-10 peers as escalating tensions in Ukraine and widespread protests in France dented sentiment toward the common currency.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Carson and Matthew Burgess

item.title: EQT Agrees to Buy Australia’s Cleanaway Waste for $6.5 Billion
item.description: EQT AB has agreed to buy Australia’s Cleanaway Waste Management Ltd. through a unit, in a deal that values the firm at about A$9.3 billion ($6.5 billion) and makes it the latest local company to enter private hands after a period of share underperformance.
item.dc:creator: Carmeli Argana

item.title: US Stock Futures Bounce After Chip Rout, Oil Slips: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures rebounded from last week’s chip rout as investors turned to earnings for direction amid mounting pressure on the artificial intelligence trade. Oil slipped.
item.dc:creator: Anand Krishnamoorthy and Matthew Burgess

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 19
item.description: Oil retreated from a five-month high, as traders weighed flareups in fighting in the Middle East against signs supply from the region is holding at near pre-war levels.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Daiichi Life Offers $4.4 Billion to Buy Rest of Challenger
item.description: Daiichi Life Group Inc. offered to buy the remainder of Challenger Ltd. that it doesn’t already own, in a takeover bid that valued the Australian firm at around A$7.9 billion ($5.5 billion).
item.dc:creator: Adam Haigh

item.title: For Three Buffetts, a $150 Billion Puzzle Over Warren’s Riches
item.description: Warren Buffett is worth an estimated $150 billion. He's also promised to divest himself of his vast wealth before he dies. Except it's hard when the pot keeps growing. So his three children are stepping in to spread it around. Alexandre Rajbhandari explains (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kioxia Shares Face Headwinds From Margin-Buying Gone Wrong
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. shares face further downward pressure because of a buildup of positions from investors who borrowed to buy the stock on the assumption it would rise, and now may need to sell at a loss.
item.dc:creator: Kentaro Tsutsumi

item.title: Traders Grow Wary of Copper Bull Market With No Sign of Tariffs
item.description: Since Donald Trump came back into office, copper has surged on a seismic reshuffling of global inventories linked to the risk that he’ll impose tariffs on the metal. But as Trump nears the halfway mark on his second term, the market’s many bulls are growing wary that prices could crash if he doesn’t follow through.
item.dc:creator: Julian Luk, Mark Burton, Alfred Cang and James Attwood

item.title: Bond Market’s Big Short Bet Gets Wakeup Call as AI Trade Wobbles
item.description: US Treasuries are showing tentative signs of reclaiming their traditional role as a haven — threatening to wrong-foot investors who are heavily positioned for this year’s bond slump to deepen.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie, Alice Gledhill and Ruth Carson

item.title: CPI Test Set to Make or Break New Zealand Dollar’s Losing Run
item.description: The New Zealand dollar has fallen for five straight quarters and if analysts are right, it may be on course to test a pandemic-era low.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Kondo and Ruth Carson

item.title: Bookmarked: News Stories On Our Reading List
item.description: Luxury travel, owls in NYC, and science competition instead of beauty pageants: Join hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo on Bloomberg This Weekend for Bookmarked, where they share stories that caught their attention over the past week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banque du Caire Seeks to Raise Up to $454 Million in Egypt IPO
item.description: Banque du Caire is looking to raise as much as 24.25 billion Egyptian pounds ($454 million) via the sale of a 30% stake, in what would be the North African country’s largest initial public offering in years.
item.dc:creator: Tarek El-Tablawy

item.title: Trump’s Latin America Allies Deepen Ties With Washington Lenders
item.description: Latin America’s rightward, market-friendly shift is reshaping its relationship with Donald Trump’s Washington, including new flows of money from the multilateral lenders historically villainized in the region for pushing fiscal austerity.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Jorgelina do Rosario

item.title: Rep. Veasey Calls for Scrutiny of Trump Russia Ties
item.description: Rep. Marc Veasey, a Texas Democrat, tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s recent moves involving Russia and Ukraine warrant greater congressional scrutiny, while warning that questions over Ukraine’s access to US military technology could undermine allies’ confidence in American defense products. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Veasey also says Tarrant County will be crucial to Democrats’ chances in Texas, arguing that strong performance there could help Senate candidate James Talarico win statewide. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chicago Tops Travelers’ Favorite US Cities
item.description: Condé Nast Traveler senior features editor Megan Spurrell tells Bloomberg This Weekend what nearly 800,000 reader votes reveal about travelers’ favorite cities, including Chicago’s enduring appeal and the rise of destinations such as Phnom Penh. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Spurrell says affordability, food, hospitality and evolving local cultures are helping both familiar destinations and less-traveled cities win devoted fans. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can America Rebuild Trust With Its Allies?
item.description: Former Canadian deputy prime minister and “Wall Street Week” contributor Chrystia Freeland and former US Treasury secretary Janet Yellen say that globalization became dangerously dependent on countries willing to weaponize trade and supply chains. Freeland recounts her shared sentiment with Yellen in her new book, “Unreliable Boyfriend.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Option Traders Brace for VIX Surge as AI Jitters Jolt Market
item.description: Accelerating US inflation and tremors across the AI sector jolted stocks in recent days, and some investors are now betting that bigger swings in tech shares will finally spread to the broader market.
item.dc:creator: Christian Dass

item.title: Rethinking America’s Faith in Innovation
item.description: Author Thomas Frank tells Bloomberg This Weekend that America’s celebration of creativity and innovation has helped justify policies that elevated white-collar knowledge work while contributing to inequality and the decline of manufacturing. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini about his new book, The Creativity Con, Frank argues that innovation is neither uniquely American nor a guarantee of broadly shared prosperity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India Cockroach Leaders Remain in Custody as Release Delayed
item.description: India’s Cockroach Janta Party raised concerns over what it described as “systematic delays and procedural obstruction” by Delhi Police and other authorities in securing the release of two of its leaders who have now spent five days in custody.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia and Rajesh Roy
